Temperature highs were exceptionally accurate across ECMWF (0.0°C error) and ICON (-0.1°C error), though ICON exhibited a strong nocturnal cold bias (-3.7°C) and GFS substantially overpredicted surface wind speeds.
narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Warm and mostly sunny conditions will dominate Kisumu and the broader Nyanza Basin today, with afternoon temperatures reaching 31°C / 88°F before evening cloudiness develops. No rain is expected today, though moderate to strong morning winds will create choppy conditions over Lake Victoria.

## Today's Forecast
High temperatures will reach 31°C / 88°F under mostly clear skies during the late morning and early afternoon, followed by developing high clouds late in the day. Overnight minimum temperatures will fall to 17°C / 63°F. Precipitation probability is below 10%, with 0.0 mm (0.00 in) expected. Winds over land will peak around 23 km/h (12 kt) from the SW in the late afternoon, with gusts up to 41 km/h (22 kt). The maximum UV index will reach 8.8 (Very High), requiring sun protection between 10:00 and 15:00. Air quality based on CAMS model guidance indicates a US AQI of 84-90 (Moderate) driven by PM2.5, as ground AQI monitoring stations are currently reporting stale data.

## Extended Outlook
Dry and warm weather will persist through Saturday, August 15th, and Sunday, August 16th, with daily high temperatures around 31°C / 88°F and minimums near 19°C / 66°F under clear to partly cloudy skies. A transition toward wetter weather is anticipated beginning Monday, August 17th, as moisture convergence increases across the Nyanza Basin. Between August 17th and August 19th (Days 3 to 5), precipitation probabilities surge to 85-100%, bringing widespread rain showers accumulating between 3.0 mm (0.12 in) and 8.6 mm (0.34 in) daily and suppressing daytime highs to 29°C / 84°F. Looking ahead to August 20th–21st (Days 6 to 7), shower activity is projected to taper into scattered light rain (1.0 mm to 4.4 mm / 0.04 to 0.17 in) with daily highs stabilizing around 29°C / 84°F to 30°C / 86°F.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
No severe thunderstorms or heavy rain hazards are expected today across Kisumu and the immediate Nyanza Basin. Very high UV radiation (peak UV index 8.8) poses a skin burn hazard during peak midday hours. Strong morning wind gusts reaching 48 km/h (26 kt) over open waters of Lake Victoria present localized wave hazards for small craft.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Boaters and fishermen on Lake Victoria should prepare for brisk south-southeasterly winds during the early morning hours, reaching sustained speeds of 32 km/h to 36 km/h (17 kt to 19 kt) from the SE with peak gusts up to 48 km/h (26 kt) from the SE between 03:00 and 09:00 EAT. These winds will generate choppy lake surface conditions. By mid-afternoon, winds will shift from the SW and ease to 19 km/h to 24 km/h (10 kt to 13 kt). No rainfall or convective squalls are expected over the lake waters today.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
The regional surface pressure field across the Nyanza Basin reflects an equatorial ridge-trough balance, with mean sea-level pressure (MSLP) averaging 1014.5 hPa to 1016.8 hPa across regional observation points. A pronounced diurnal pressure cycle is active, dropping from a morning peak near 1018.0 hPa down to an afternoon thermal troughing low of 1006.6 hPa to 1009.7 hPa across Kisumu and surrounding lowlands. This thermal troughing drives the lake-breeze circulation, shifting surface winds from morning southeasterlies to afternoon southwesterlies. Low mid-level convective available potential energy (CAPE < 100 J/kg) and dry air aloft keep convective initiation suppressed today.

All ground air quality monitoring stations in Kisumu reported stale readings (>5 hours old): Kisumu Airport (PM2.5: 59.0 µg/m³, PM10: 15.0 µg/m³), Ochieng' Avenue (PM2.5: 50.0 µg/m³, PM10: 18.0 µg/m³), and Dunga Beach (PM2.5: 70.0 µg/m³, PM10: 37.0 µg/m³). Because no active ground station provided a fresh reading, current air quality assessment relies entirely on CAMS model guidance, which indicates Moderate air quality (US AQI 84-90).

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Forecaster confidence for today's dry and warm call is high across all models. Recent verification from August 13th demonstrated that GFS, ICON, and UKMO accurately identified rainfall events, while ECMWF suffered a false-dry miss. However, for maximum temperatures, ECMWF (0.0°C error) and ICON (-0.1°C error) remain superior to UKMO (+1.3°C error). ICON's persistent overnight low-temperature cold bias (-3.7°C) has been compensated for by blending toward ECMWF and GFS low temperature guidance (17°C call). GFS continues to overpredict surface wind magnitudes by 15 km/h to 21 km/h; thus, surface wind calls have been adjusted using ICON and Best Match guidance. For the extended outlook (Days 3–7), track records currently show zero completed verification checks, introducing higher uncertainty for the mid-week rain onset signal on August 17th.
